Mutation testing evaluates tests against seeded faults; passing an injected-fault audit does not establish general fault detection. Research finds correlation between mutant and real-fault detection, but questions whether ML mutations consistently represent implementation bugs. For NextItNet, the methodological recommendation is to separate injection verification from probe scoring: independently inspect executed indices and tensor dependencies, record a concrete witness, then run the frozen diagnostic without exposing mutation identity. Never define successful injection by the diagnostic’s own alarm. [Real-fault study](https://homes.cs.washington.edu/~mernst/pubs/mutation-effectiveness-fse2014-abstract.html), [ML mutation critique](https://pure.tudelft.nl/ws/portalfiles/portal/95548898/What_Are_We_Really_Testing_in_Mutation_Testing_for_Machine_Learning_A_Critical_Reflection.pdf).

For left-padded readout, use position-coded synthetic features and varied nonempty history lengths: independently verify selection of the final nonpadding index, versus `count_nonzero−1`. Full-length histories can conceal the mutation. For future leakage, independently verify an active forbidden dependency; separately test the causal relation that changing a suffix cannot change earlier features or scores, with dropout disabled and numerical tolerances fixed. Test intermediate positions because final-position inference alone cannot expose future access. Distinguish installed faults, independently witnessed behavioral effects, and probe detections. Unmanifested mutants remain unresolved; survival on finite inputs does not prove equivalence. These audit recommendations follow NextItNet’s causal sequence contract. [NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf).

Freeze probes and thresholds before evaluating held-out operator families, alternative implementations, and documented real bugs. Report injection failures, unresolved cases, conditional detection rates, and clean-control false alarms separately. Transfer claims require evidence beyond design-time mutants; realistic fault generation remains a central mutation-testing concern. [DeepMutation](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/deepmutation-a-neural-mutation-tool/).
